idea: Veto is a spending firewall for AI agent wallets on NEAR. An agent with a key is either unbounded (one prompt injection drains the balance) or chained to a human on every payment (no longer an agent). Veto is the third option: the owner writes a policy - per-transaction, daily and monthly caps, counterparty allow/deny lists, an approval threshold, velocity limits, allowed action kinds, swap venue/slippage/destination pins, expiry and a pause switch - and every agent action is judged before money moves. Three independent layers enforce it. An off-chain engine runs ~20 checks per decision with exact bigint arithmetic, deny-by-default and reserved budget for pending approvals, and explains every refusal with a reason code. A Rust contract holds the funds and recomputes the limits on-chain; the agent's key is a function-call key scoped to spend(), so a stolen key cannot add keys, withdraw or pause. A human approval queue re-evaluates the policy at execution time, so an approval granted under yesterday's limits cannot be used today. Every decision, including refusals, lands in a hash-chained audit log whose head is anchored on-chain, and a refused spend reverts the transaction while emitting a NEP-297 deny event with the reason code. NEAR specifics: real NEAR Intents (1Click) quotes are validated before a swap - venue, slippage, quote expiry and a destination pinned to the agent's own MPC-derived chain-signature address from v1.signer. Verified live on testnet: deploy, policy install, one allowed spend, one reverted overspend, one key-level refusal. 85 tests, 29 adversarial escape attempts with asserted verdicts, and 28 conformance checks against the deployed contract; no wallet, key or funds needed to reproduce.
